original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Fixed nonabelian S3 paid alphabet of #4351: no shared word of total cost at most two writes the transposition (1 3) on any register, for any number of scratch registers.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a nonabelian register model escapes the three-register obstruction. #4351 supplies one exact S3 paid alphabet and a screen; this package answers its shared-length-two sub-question at that fixed alphabet. It claims no register-model escape, target identity or paid saving.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the nonabelian register-model route: it closes the cheapest sharing escape (total cost two) for one exact alphabet. The length-three target screen and every native/paid conversion remain open. No kappa, supplier admission or selected-frontier change is claimed.
stop_rule: Stop after the all-size subadditivity proof, the complete cost-at-most-two enumeration and the cost-three and shared cost-four controls. Do not search length three or a different alphabet.
evidence: PROOF.md proves the all-size word-norm bound. verify.py rebuilds S3, checks subadditivity on all 36 ordered pairs, enumerates 272 shared words at total cost at most two on two and three registers (768 register evaluations), and asserts cost-3 attainment, shared cost-4 scratch restoration and two mutation controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a different shared-call cost model break the word-norm bound?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If one paid call can carry different alphabet elements on different registers for one unit, the induced element is not a subsequence product.
open_questions.first_step: State that model exact cost and enumerate its cost-two calls.
open_questions.blocked_by: The cost is undefined in #4351, so no lower bound can be claimed for that model.

open_questions.question: Can the same norm obstruction be combined with a target screen at length three or more?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A cost-three word attains (1 3), so a whole diagonal target is the next place a sharing gain could appear.
open_questions.first_step: Pin one target and count shared letters against its representation rank.
open_questions.blocked_by: No native conversion or supplier instance is supplied by #4351 or this package.
